changes.purpose: persistent one-row-per-case admission table and web grants

new_state_necessity.why: one durable row per owner/case is required to prevent a failed/new-message retry from creating a second Run after restart; existing web_requests has no owner+case uniqueness and retention can retire it
columns: run_id UNIQUE for one Run per case
binding JSONB for exact scope audit
new_state_necessity.no_new_ledger: three admitted Runs x original per-Run 8 calls/18,000 units is the 24/54,000 global ceiling; no second global budget ledger

admission_semantics.permit_trust: only the trusted operator starts the private HostPolicy with smoke_admission_file; the permit is HMAC-signed with DATAPILOT_SMOKE_ADMISSION_KEY, which is not in the host file, browser, model or MCP env; approved_by_role and source approval ref are inside the signed body
admission_semantics.one_run_per_case: PRIMARY KEY(owner,case_id); second message for same case rejected; failed case cannot be retried with a new key
admission_semantics.same_request_retry: same request SHA + message returns the original run; no new command
admission_semantics.fourth_or_replacement: only exactly 3 signed cases match; fourth request/other dataset/version/corpus rejected
admission_semantics.owner_scope: owner, question SHA, metric/semantic/dataset, full window, report/rag policy, corpus/index/document and required-fact bindings checked against payload
admission_semantics.expiry_stop: permit expiry and STOP file checked on every gate; permit hash change rejects existing Run; campaign 1800s is shared from min(admitted_at) for the permit
admission_semantics.restart: admission row is committed with the original Web transaction; restart re-reads the row and permit
admission_semantics.unknown: existing run/ledger unknown-outcome handling remains; admission never creates a replacement Run
admission_semantics.normal_fake: gate disabled when smoke_admission_file is absent; existing Fake tests pass
admission_semantics.limits: per-Run wall-clock 180s is an authorization/stop condition, not a hard process-kill wall clock; existing 30s provider timeout and step/SQL limits remain
